thread.title_full: Foster mother to be charged with murder in death of missing 10-year-old girl, sources say - NewsBreak

author: Madeleine Wright
title: Foster mother to be charged with murder in death of missing 10-year-old girl, sources say - NewsBreak
text:
By Madeleine Wright Joe Holden ,
11 hours ago
The foster mother of Jalayshia Allford will be charged with murder after the 10-year-old's body was found inside a car Thursday morning in New Jersey, sources said.
Police found Allford's body inside a car Thursday morning in Camden County, sources said.
Law enforcement sources said Allford was beaten to death. It's unclear if any weapon has been recovered.
Krasner, Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel and other officials are expected to share an update and announce murder charges in the case Thursday at 5:30 p.m.
Another person who is alleged to have provided the location of Allford's body could also face charges, according to sources. It's unclear if that will happen Thursday.
Allford has been missing since Oct. 26 and was last seen on North Simpson Street in West Philadelphia, according to police.
Her body was found in the trunk of a car near the Stonington Court Apartments in Lindenwold early Thursday morning, law enforcement sources told CBS News Philadelphia. Police have not revealed how she died.
Conflicting information from family members "stunted" the investigation and search efforts, law enforcement sources told CBS News Philadelphia. Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said his office was involved in the investigation due to legal obstacles, but he did not provide details.
Family members said her foster mother told relatives the girl had gone to her biological mother's home. But those family members stated the biological mother did not have visitation rights and Jalayshia was not at her home.
Investigators searched a backyard dumpster in Lower Merion Township for clues to Jalayshia's disappearance Tuesday night, sources said.
The FBI went to the foster mother's home on North Simpson Street Tuesday night with a search warrant. After no one answered the door, agents forced their way inside.
People tied pink and white balloons outside the West Philadelphia home where Jalayshia lived with a foster mother as news of her death spread Thursday afternoon.
"For me to come out here to something like this is very devastating," Tyeisha Stots said. "I was sad last night. I couldn't sleep."
"It was a lot of hope. We had a lot of people out here searching," Jimmy Ligon of West Philadelphia said. "We had a lot of people. At least 50 people came out yesterday to search."
For some, the loss feels personal.
Valerie Brown said Jalayshia went to camp with her son.
"I'm feeling hurt. I'm feeling — my spirit is heavy," Brown said. "I have a lot of knots in my stomach and you know, it just hits very close to home for me."
West Philly community members will hold a prayer vigil outside the foster home on North Simpson Street at 6 p.m.
This is a developing story. Check back for updates.
